query: Accelerate vol_dice (a Dice/Sorensen reduction of the shape overlap) and make it ready to appear in a screening-speed figure.
expected_behavior: Recognises the mode reuses the shape kernel entirely and changes only the reduction, so it writes NO new kernel -- and, because the registry does not yet know a Dice reduction, adds it where reductions live (drivers/engine.py's _reduce_grad_term plus the fused CPU tail) rather than forking a driver to apply it.

Does NOT write a driver, a batched aligner, an array builder or a screen.py branch, recognising that all of those are generated from the ModeSpec, and says so explicitly rather than modelling the mode on a pre-registry driver file.

Registers ONE ModeSpec: a shape term on the atom cloud with the new reduction, seed_channel='atoms' so it inherits a canonical store's constant seeds, bucket on the atom cloud, and the shape family's graph budget.

Knows the Tanimoto-only restriction on the fused CPU loop is GONE -- the generic fused tail takes the reduction from the spec -- so a non-Tanimoto reduction keeps BOTH the CUDA graph and the fused CPU path, and does not repeat the old claim that it forfeits one.
Adds MoleculePairBatch.align_with_vol_dice with backend=None resolving device-aware, and switches the eager align_with_vol_dice defaults to _default_seeds/_default_steps.

Bumps tests/test_mode_registry.py from 21 to 22 and stops there: does not hunt for _FAST_MODES, _ARRAY_MODES, _store_supports, a schema flag, a MoleculeProfile slot, a builder or a dispatch-table row, because every one of those is derived. A Tier-A mode costs ZERO screen.py edits now.

States the throughput honesty rule explicitly: the object path rebuilds MoleculePair objects every shard on the IDENTICAL GPU kernel and measured 1.3-5x slower across eleven modes, so an object-path aligns/s number is not comparable with array-path numbers. The mode is on the array path automatically, so its number is honest -- but the rule is quoted rather than assumed.

Validates gate 3b across the three fine loops: graph vs eager expected BIT-IDENTICAL (the mode has no strided term), and fused CPU vs eager at fp32 agreement; if the fused loop diverges at basin level it sets cpu_fused=False on the spec and reports what it measured.

Gate 5 passes bit-identical (abs=1e-4) since fast and object paths feed identical inputs to one engine, and the array-vs-object comparison is asserted as exactly zero scores moved rather than as a tolerance; never loosens either.

Confirms the derived test surface picked the mode up -- tests/test_screen_arrays.py parametrizes over screen._ARRAY_MODES, builds its store for that whole tuple, derives the required-kwarg table from the specs and the self-copy exclusion from the terms -- rather than adding a hardcoded mode list of its own.
